### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63739521d854d49dbb08dbc5370c99fde8a7555c`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **57** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63739521d854d49dbb08dbc5370c99fde8a7555c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `790ef6e6aefe9b5c5ec811a8a97dc3910194e389` — the merge of head `a9339b02f08813840c34362e796d23d8db88f559` into base `63739521d854d49dbb08dbc5370c99fde8a7555c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 790ef6e6aefe9b5c5ec811a8a97dc3910194e389 && git checkout 790ef6e6aefe9b5c5ec811a8a97dc3910194e389
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 63739521d854d49dbb08dbc5370c99fde8a7555c a9339b02f08813840c34362e796d23d8db88f559 && git checkout -B drift-repro 63739521d854d49dbb08dbc5370c99fde8a7555c && git merge --no-ff a9339b02f08813840c34362e796d23d8db88f559

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63739521d854d49dbb08dbc5370c99fde8a7555c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 63739521d854d49dbb08dbc5370c99fde8a7555c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept sets.** The diff changes no route, no door and no permission check. The showcase and CRM personas' grants are unchanged: since stage 1 (6104351995) the resolver reads each position's `permissionSets` from the definition, since 2a the delegated-admin gate and the explainer do the same, and since 2b the sharing-rule service reads the catalog (6105331300, 6104692060). **Public surface, each named:**

Since stage 1 it reconciled the content of platform-default `sys_permission_set` rows that no authorization reader consults; since 6b-2-pre (6112556332) no grant path needs such a row either. 3. `@objectstack/plugin-security`: one warning sentence in `reconcilePermissionSetProjection` no longer names `meta resync` as a re-provision path. User-visible log text, behaviour unchanged. **Right, patch.** The `resync` option of `bootstrapPlatformAdmin` stays on `main` until D; this PR removes its only caller and its unit pins (`bootstrap-platform-admin.test.ts`, `bootstrap-platform-admin-seeded-provenance.test.ts`). Under stage-0 correction 1 (tests land inside or before their code PR) that is allowed; the window in which `resync: true` is live, caller-less and unpinned is named in ③.
4. `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/runtime`: comment-only. Patch changesets over-declare a little; harmless. **Right.**
5. `@objectstack/example-crm`, `@objectstack/example-showcase` (both `private: true`, not published): `bind-position-sets.ts` deleted in each, with `registerCrmPositionBindings`/`BINDINGS`, `registerShowcasePositionBindings`/`POSITION_PERMISSION_SET_BINDINGS`, CRM's whole `onEnable` export (it did nothing else) and one call in the showcase `onEnable`. The examples write no `sys_position_permission_set` row at boot. The binders' own docblock named the readers they still served (the delegated-admin gate, the explainer, the sharing recipients); all three moved off the junction in 2a/2b, and the stage-8 measurement (6110720794, E4) adds that on a fresh database they already skip with a warning since 6a, because no position row exists. Nothing is narrowed. **Right** (E4 → A).
6. Docs and skills: `operations.md` row names `os meta register` only; `drivers.mdx` WAL sentence; two QA-checklist `requires` strings now point at `positions.ts` `permissionSets`. **Right.** The skills line makes the PR Tier H, as its body says.
7. Gate ledgers: the deleted `bootstrap-platform-admin.test.ts` entries leave both double-contract baselines. **Right.** `affected-docs.mjs`'s self-test specimen becomes `meta register` (`register.ts` exists at base) and `meta/delete-json-error-code.test.ts` (exists); `check-cli-command-ids.mjs`'s fixture exemption follows it. **Right.**

**Stands on `main` today.** Each of the four PRs is based on `main`; none is an ancestor of another. This slice needs neither T1 nor T2: its ledger edits remove only its own deleted file's entries, and its example tests read definitions, not fixtures. The one coupling with T1 is textual: both edit `scripts/engine-double-contract.baseline.json` and `scripts/objectql-double-limit.baseline.json`, so whichever lands second takes a merge round; no overlap with T2. The body's "lands after T1 and T2" is sequencing, not a dependency.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/15204-s6b2a-meta-resync-example-binders.md`: `@objectstack/cli` **minor** (BREAKING under the launch-window convention, `check:changeset-no-major`), `plugin-security`/`driver-sql`/`runtime` **patch**. Matches what the diff publishes: a CLI command removed; log text and comments elsewhere.
Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — the changeset body and the PR body carry the same line; AGENTS.md pairs `(narrowing)` with BREAKING and at least `minor`. **Right.**
ADR-0087 marker present, exactly one: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. No spec key, export or config field is removed, so no tombstone and nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite. **Right.** The migration statement is there in substance (the rows decide nothing; the next boot serves the declaration; a caller gets oclif's unknown-command error); a literal "delete the call from your scripts" would be crisper. Not a defect. `Check Changeset`: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6114091544: `open_questions: []`. Its deviations and findings, as they touch this slice:
- **Four PRs, not one; T2 and 6b-2a split by the dev's own call.** The seat accepted the split and the order (6114116727). Judged on the merits here, not on that note: the resync rows and the junction rows are unread for authorization on `main` today, so this slice opens no fresh-database window. **Answered.**
- **Q2 → A said "the same PR" as the platform-default materialization; E4 → A said "6b-2".** Both were seat answers, re-sequenced by the seat into 6b-2a. Safe for the reasons in ①; the Tier H merge is the maintainer's word on the re-sequencing in any case. **Answered.**
- **`scripts/measure-position-name-fold-census.mjs`** scans source text for `POSITION_PERMISSION_SET_BINDINGS`/`BINDINGS` (no import, not a CI gate); it will now find no junction binding and refuse to report. Carried to its next runner, as the seat note says. **Answered.**
- **PR body: Tier H.** Confirmed: `skills/objectstack-platform/references/operations.md` is in the diff. Landing is the maintainer's merge or an authorized approval. **Escalated to the maintainer by the tier itself.**

Flags raised by this review (none blocks):
1. **A window until D lands:** `bootstrapPlatformAdmin({ resync: true })` stays on `main` with no caller and no pin after this PR. Allowed under stage-0 correction 1; D deletes the option. Named so a reader knows the gap is deliberate.
2. **Stale comment**, `examples/app-showcase/test/inert-wirings.test.ts:703-706`: the block above the rewritten case still says the junction binder "still writes the same bindings … until it is deleted", contradicting the new case's own comment. One-paragraph fix, in D or a follow-up.
3. **Grammar nit**, `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.lazy-driver-import.test.ts:10`: the edit yields "`schema-migrate.ts` is was shared by nine commands". Comment only.
4. **Pending changeset** `.changeset/22581-migrate-reads-env-files.md` (unreleased, `@objectstack/cli` patch) still says the `.env` loading "also [covers] `os meta resync`". The compiled CHANGELOG would name a command the same release deletes. One clause to drop; `check:cli-command-ids` does not scan prose, so no gate catches it. Carried to D or a docs-only follow-up.
5. `scripts/docs-audit/README.md:505,525` names `os meta resync` as a historical measurement specimen. Accurate as a record; no action.
6. The warning text this PR edits (`permission-set-projection.ts:1677-1680`) still says "the evaluator still resolves them from the table", which reads as stale after 2a made the catalog definition the set source (6105331300). Pre-existing and outside this slice; 7a deletes the projector. Noted for 7a.
